description: Redwood Inference will run a focused lifecycle growth experiments sprint to lift activation (first successful production-like inference call) and early retention (repeat usage in week 1–2) for self-serve and PLG-led developers. The sprint tests three levers in parallel: (1) onboarding email sequences (welcome, quickstart, first-success, troubleshooting, and “next step” emails), (2) in-console nudges (setup checklist, contextual banners, and just-in-time prompts tied to missing activation steps like API key creation, first request, enabling streaming, viewing latency/cost dashboards), and (3) retargeting for non-activated signups and recently lapsed users (e.g., LinkedIn/Google with developer-first messaging and benchmark proof points). Success will be measured via an agreed event taxonomy and experiment framework: activation rate within 24h/72h, time-to-first-success, D7/D14 retention, and conversion to higher-intent milestones (adding billing, increasing token usage, creating a deployment/route, inviting teammates). Guardrails include email deliverability/unsubscribes, support ticket volume, and SLO-impact checks for any console changes. Stakeholders include Growth Marketing (Ben Carter) + Marketing Ops (Tyler Benson) for campaign execution and attribution; Product (Marissa Cole, Paula Mendes, Henry Cho) for console experience and telemetry requirements; Design (Tessa Morgan, Kenji Nakamura, Alicia Perez) for nudge UX and messaging; Engineering (Jada Williams, Jin Woo Park) for instrumentation and experimentation primitives; and Sales/CS (Avery Johnson, Aparna Reddy) for feedback loops on activation blockers that signal sales-assist triggers. Timeline: Week 0 setup (tracking + copy + UX specs), Week 1 launch (email v1 + console nudge v1 + retargeting audiences), Week 2 iterate (A/B variants + bug fixes), Week 3 readout and decision (roll-forward, rollback, or new hypotheses) with a documented learnings report and next-sprint backlog.
